evals.prompt: We run Petshop Mikroulis (petshop-mikroulis.gr), a Greek online pet-supplies shop. Nikos, our marketing guy, hand-copied our last six full weeks of Search Console clicks and impressions into evals/files/gsc-clicks-baseline-petshop-mikroulis-en.md — no tools are connected in this session, that paste is the entire data set. Set up our organic-traffic alert thresholds using the standard-deviation method from your threshold guide: actual numbers we can drop into our monitoring spreadsheet, with each alert level explained. Heads up: July 8 was a confirmed hosting outage (we got a service credit for it), so handle that day properly. Also, our old agency alerted us at -30% week-over-week because 'that's the industry standard' — is that right for us? And tell us whether our CTR is in the normal range for pet e-commerce.
evals.expected_output: A threshold configuration built solely from the six-week paste: the 2026-07-08 outage day (41 clicks) excluded from the baseline as a known-cause outlier with the exclusion stated, baseline means computed for named populations (≈310 weekday / ≈206 weekend / ≈1,967 weekly totals), Info/Warning/Critical/Emergency levels derived from the computed variation via the guide's SD ladder with visible arithmetic, the -30% WoW figure repositioned as a generic default far looser than this site's measured variance rather than 'the industry standard' for this site, the regular weekend dip handled like-for-like so Saturdays never grade against a weekday mean, the CTR question answered from the fixture (≈3.4%) with no invented pet-industry benchmark, and every number either fixture-traced or visibly derived.
expectations: The 2026-07-08 outage day (41 clicks) is identified as the fixture's known-cause anomaly and excluded from the baseline per the threshold guide's baseline steps ('Remove known outliers (holidays, outages, one-time events)'), with the exclusion stated in the output rather than silently applied, and the day is not re-diagnosed as an unexplained SEO problem — the prompt and fixture both say the hosting outage is confirmed.

Baseline arithmetic is fixture-exact for whichever population the response names (the population is defined before averaging): a weekday-clicks mean falls in 309-312 (the 29 clean Mon-Fri values), a weekend mean in 205-207 (the 12 Sat-Sun values), a weekly-totals mean in 1,966-1,968 (the five clean weeks 1,972/1,971/1,973/1,977/1,943 with the outage week excluded), an all-clean-days mean in 279-281 (41 values) — each stated mean carrying its population and visible derivation, and a mean matching none of these populations fails.

Alert levels are justified from the fixture's measured variance per the guide's standard-deviation ladder (Info/Warning/Critical/Emergency at 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3 standard deviations from the baseline mean — the method the prompt requests): a standard deviation actually computed from fixture values anchors the levels (weekday SD ≈11-12, weekend SD ≈10-12, weekly-totals SD ≈12-14, or all-clean-days SD ≈48-50, matching the stated population — a mixed weekday/weekend SD must then be paired with the like-for-like handling the day-of-week discipline expectation requires, since a 1σ band of 280±49 grades Saturdays against weekdays), the multiplier-to-level mapping is shown, and no threshold number appears that is neither fixture-derived arithmetic nor an explicitly labeled generic default.

The old agency's '-30% week-over-week industry standard' is answered with threshold sanity, not deference: -30% is identified as the generic default from the skill's own quick-reference table, shown to be far looser than this site's measured variance, with the comparison arithmetic visible and its population named: on weekly totals a -30% week is ≈590 clicks below the ≈1,967 mean (0.30 × 1,967 = 590), i.e. on the order of 40+ standard deviations (43σ at the sample SD 13.7, 48σ at the population SD 12.3), so smaller-but-real losses would never alert; an equivalent demonstration on a daily population passes (≈93 clicks below the ≈310 weekday mean, ≈8σ) — what fails is presenting -30% as derived from this site's data, or asserting looseness without arithmetic — and -30% is kept, if at all, only as an explicitly labeled backstop default.

Day-of-week discipline follows the guide's note ('Compare Monday to Monday, not Monday to Sunday') and weekend suppression rule: the configuration prevents the fixture's regular weekend dip (weekend days run roughly a third below weekdays — ≈206 vs ≈310) from firing false alerts, via like-for-like same-weekday comparison, separate weekday/weekend baselines, or the guide's weekend adjustment, with the chosen mechanism named.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every clicks, impressions, and CTR figure traces to the fixture or is arithmetic derived solely from fixture numbers with the derivation visible (clean-weeks CTR ≈3.38% aggregated over the five clean weeks, per-week CTR 3.35-3.41 — the five clean weeks run 3.3508%-3.4041%; any rounding of those values passes — with the outage week's ≈2.83 as the anomaly); the pet-e-commerce 'normal range' question is answered without inventing an industry benchmark — the fixture contains none, so any external norm appears only as an explicitly labeled generic estimate not derived from this data — hedging words alone ('probably', 'typically around') are not such a label (same standard as eval 5) — or the honest answer names what would supply it; no sessions, revenue, ranking, or per-day impression figures appear (the fixture has none), and sources are labeled per the Output Validation item 'Every metric cites its data source and collection date'.

evals.prompt: Alert cleanup for petshop-mikroulis.gr, please. The agency we used until 2024 left us an alert setup that is drowning us — Nikos now ignores the alert inbox completely, which scares me more than the alerts do. The full config table plus a 30-day fire log with our own notes on which fires were actually worth acting on is in evals/files/alert-config-review-petshop-mikroulis-en.md. No tools are connected — that file is everything we can export. Review and optimize: which alerts do we keep, fix, retune, or kill, and why? Two specific questions: (1) the Core Web Vitals rows have never fired — are they even working? (2) can we just delete the 'unlinked brand mention' alert? If there is no link, there is nothing to get, right?
evals.expected_output: An alert-fatigue triage grounded in the config and log: the FID row flagged as monitoring a metric retired in March 2024 and replaced with an INP rule at the 200 ms boundary, the LCP rule's 2.0 s corrected to the 2.5 s Good threshold and the CLS 0.1 row kept as already correct, the FAQ rich-result alert retired because the rich results and the reporting that fed it were cut — without advising removal of FAQPage markup itself — the log read honestly (10 actionable of 160 fires, roughly 94% noise against the guide's >30% too-tight signal), the ±1-position rank alert widened to tiered thresholds with batching and cooldown instead of deleted outright, the weekend-heavy traffic fires fixed like-for-like while the one true positive (the 08/07 outage) is honored, the four zero-fire rows named dead sensors, missing security and site-down criticals added, and the unlinked-mention alert kept as a scored entity/GEO signal at digest priority rather than deleted as worthless.
expectations: The FID row is flagged as a config defect per settled ruling R4 (docs/loop/SETTLED-RULINGS.md): FID was retired in March 2024, so an alert on 'FID > 100 ms' monitors a dead metric — which also explains its zero fires (the log's own note says the FID column disappeared from the tools) — and the fix replaces it with an INP rule at the 200 ms Good boundary; nothing in the response treats FID as a live metric to keep, retune, or wait on, and if the response quotes a config row it quotes it verbatim.

The LCP and CLS boundaries land on ruling R4's exact values: the config's 'LCP > 2.0 s' trigger is corrected to the 2.5 s Good threshold (the 2.0 s figure circulates from vendor sources, not Google — noting that provenance is a plus, not required), the CLS row's 0.1 boundary is recognized as already correct and is not 'fixed' into a different number, and the corrected CWV alert set uses LCP 2.5 s / INP 200 ms / CLS 0.1 as its Good-threshold boundaries (a second severity tier at the Poor levels, e.g. LCP 4 s, may sit on top, never instead).

The FAQ rich-result alert is retired per settled ruling R3: Google cut FAQ rich results and the Search Console reporting that fed such an alert in 2026 — the log's zero fires since early 2026 confirm the sensor is dead — so the alert is removed rather than retuned, no replacement FAQ-rich-result monitoring is proposed, and the response does NOT extend the retirement into advising removal of FAQPage markup itself. That last clause is graded on both legs and neither passes alone (R297 pairing). MUST APPEAR: the keep-reason the ruling actually licenses — the markup is valid schema.org, costs nothing to keep, and Google's own guidance is that there is no need to proactively remove it. Silence is not a pass: retiring the alert without saying why the markup nonetheless stays leaves the advice indistinguishable from 'remove the markup too'. MUST NOT APPEAR: the retention justified by an AI-engine/GEO parsing, answer-engine-extraction or AI-citation benefit — and that rationale must not be attributed to the house ruling, which is the opposite of what the house ruling says: R3 amendment 9a retracted the clause 'its value is AI-engine/GEO parsing' as having no primary source either way, so keeping the markup for that reason fails on the same ground as advising its deletion.

Fatigue arithmetic defines its population before counting: across the nine config rows over the 30-day log window (2026-07-05 to 2026-08-03) there were 160 fires with 10 marked actionable, so any stated noise or false-positive rate falls in 92-95% with the 150-of-160 derivation visible, judged against the tuning guide's signal 'Too many false positives (>30% of alerts are noise)' — this config is far past too-tight — and Nikos ignoring the inbox is named as exactly the alert-fatigue failure the skill's own tip warns about ('Too many alerts = ignored alerts').

The two noisiest rules are retuned with reasoning, not deleted into a coverage hole: the ±1-position rule (118 fires, 6 actionable, across the 140 tracked keywords) is widened to tiered thresholds consistent with the guide's ranking table (Tier-1 warning at drops >=3 and critical at >=5, looser tiers below) plus batching/digest delivery and a duplicate cooldown per the suppression rules, keeping ranking coverage alive; and the day-over-day traffic rule's 8-of-9 weekend fires are diagnosed as a like-for-like failure (weekend dips graded against weekday levels) with the fix drawn from the guide — weekend adjustment or same-weekday comparison — while its one actionable fire (Wed 08/07, the confirmed hosting outage) is acknowledged as a true positive that justifies keeping a retuned day-over-day rule.

Estate triage names its populations: exactly 4 of the nine config rows fired zero times in the window (FID, LCP, CLS, FAQ) and are identified as dead sensors — for the LCP/CLS rows because the feeding subscription lapsed in March 2026, so the fix requires rewiring a data source (e.g. a page-speed check or ~~search console when available), not just editing thresholds — the SSL rule's 1-fire/1-actionable record marks it a keeper, missing Critical coverage is added per the templates (at minimum a security/manual-action alert at any-detection and a site-down/5xx alert), and the unlinked-mention deletion request is answered per settled ruling R5: unlinked brand mentions are a scored entity/GEO visibility signal (CITE item I09). PASS requires both that the response affirms that value (rejecting the prompt's 'nothing to get' premise) and that the signal keeps a capture path — a weekly digest, Opportunity priority, or a reclamation worklist; retiring the immediate email while keeping the signal passes. FAIL is endorsing the premise, calling the mentions worthless, or dropping them with no capture path anywhere.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every fire count, date, threshold, and condition traces to the fixture's config table and log, derived rates carry visible arithmetic from fixture numbers only, and no current site metrics are invented — the fixture contains no current LCP/INP/CLS measurements, no rankings, and no traffic values, so the response proposes how to re-measure rather than asserting today's values, and no ~~SEO tool, ~~search console, or ~~page speed tool output is simulated.

Ο Νίκος περνάει κάθε πρωί με το χέρι τις θέσεις των 12 πιο σημαντικών λέξεών μας σε ένα αρχείο — οι μετρήσεις 03/08 έως 07/08, το απόσπασμα από το uptime monitor και μια σημείωση για το τι άλλαξε στο site βρίσκονται στο evals/files/rank-log-incident-petshop-mikroulis-el.md. Κανένα εργαλείο δεν είναι συνδεδεμένο — αυτό το αρχείο είναι ό,τι έχουμε. Σήμερα, 07/08, χτύπησαν οι ειδοποιήσεις μας: οι λέξεις της κατηγορίας σκύλου βουλιάζουν μέρα με τη μέρα, και την Τετάρτη 05/08 η λέξη «άμμος γάτας» εξαφανίστηκε τελείως από το εργαλείο. Γράψε την απάντηση στα ελληνικά.
evals.expected_output: A Greek-language incident triage that separates artifact from incident: the one-day «—» on «άμμος γάτας» read as a probable tracking artifact (the tool's 05/08 maintenance notice plus the return to position 7 on 06/08) to verify with a cheap check rather than escalate, the three dog-food keywords identified as the genuine Critical incident — drops of 12, 13, and 10 positions vs 03/08, sustained across three consecutive snapshots, all landing on /trofes-skylou/ — sequenced detect → verify → diagnose → escalate with the uptime excerpt's HTTP 500 windows from 04/08 22:41, the homepage's clean 100%, and the 03/08 filter-plugin deploy held as the leading hypothesis rather than proven fact, the developer engaged same-day through the emergency-grade path with the specific evidence and the owner informed, the eight stable keywords left alone, and the mechanical Greek layer clean with fluency judged by the binding editor pass.
expectations: The «άμμος γάτας» reading is triaged artifact-first with honest uncertainty: of the 12 tracked keywords it is the only one with a missing measurement (the 05/08 «—»), the response connects it to the fixture's tool-maintenance notice for that morning and to the unchanged position 7 on 04/08 and 06/08, classifies it a probable tracking artifact rather than a real loss, prescribes a cheap verification (a manual search check or the next reading) instead of a recovery plan, does not assert the artifact explanation as confirmed fact, and if it quotes the tool's maintenance notice it quotes it verbatim.

The genuine incident is counted with its rule stated: exactly 3 of the 12 tracked keywords — «ξηρά τροφή σκύλου», «τροφή σκύλου grain free», «τροφή κουταβιού» — show drops that persist across the 05/08, 06/08, and 07/08 snapshots rather than one-day blips, the 03/08→07/08 deltas are fixture-derived with visible arithmetic — 12, 13, and 10 positions respectively; a figure presented as the 03/08→07/08 change for one of these three keywords and lying outside 10-13 fails, while intermediate day-over-day or partial-window deltas may also appear provided each names its comparison period — all three are mapped to the shared landing page /trofes-skylou/, the incident is graded Critical consistent with the Tier-1 rules (each drop far exceeds the >=5 critical threshold and the fixture tiers these keywords Tier 1), and none of the 8 stable keywords is manufactured into a problem.

The response runs an ordered incident sequence — detect, verify, diagnose, escalate — in the playbook's shape: verification precedes diagnosis (confirming the category page's live state and indexation via named checks such as loading the URL and a site: query, proposed as checks to run, not reported as results), and the diagnosis is built from the fixture's own evidence — the uptime excerpt's HTTP 500 windows on /trofes-skylou/ starting 04/08 22:41 while the homepage held 100% availability, the server-log climb from 0 (03/08) to 44/51/47 daily 500 responses, and the 03/08 evening filter-plugin deploy per the playbook's review-recent-deployments step — with the plugin framed as the leading hypothesis consistent with the timeline, not asserted as proven root cause.

Escalation is concrete on who, when, and with what: the external developer is engaged the same day at the top of the P0-P3 response axis (the templates' P0 clock — immediate: acknowledge under 15 minutes, first action within the hour — or at least P1's same-day resolution, rather than a routine 48-hour or same-week tier; naming the contrast is a plus, not required, since this fixture states no contractor SLA), handed a specific evidence package (the category URL, the 500 timestamps or daily counts, the deploy timing, the rank deltas), whoever owns the business decision is named as kept informed (a role is enough — this fixture names no owner), and the user's how-worried-should-we-be question gets a calibrated answer — urgent action on the category incident, no alarm on the «άμμος γάτας» artifact pending its verification.

Greek output quality (watch-item W4 guard, docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md), mechanical layer plus the binding editor's verdict: the response is written in Greek with correct diacritics and final-sigma use throughout, no untranslated English boilerplate section headings (technical tokens stay as-is — HTTP 500, URLs, Tier 1, uptime, plugin, site:), and none of the anti-slop §6 ruled Greek regression forms recurs — e.g. the «Όλα τα [0-9]» totality-with-numeral calque (the native shape is «Και οι τρεις λέξεις…» or a restructure) — for this eval the gender/spelled-out variants are in scope and must be checked too: «Όλες οι τρεις», «Όλα τα τρία», «Όλες οι 3» are barred alongside it in the client-facing Greek prose (the digit grep alone does not cover them; no phrasing is prescribed, only these calque forms are barred) — or agency-provenance placeholders inside client-facing text. This expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on this eval's Greek output (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). That grade decides fluency, idiomatic naturalness, translation-ese and register, and where any clause above names fluency, naturalness or register it decides that clause too — this grader forms no second opinion on it. PASS = the mechanical clauses above hold AND the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL, or any mechanical clause above is breached. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). The editor's report is the only evidence that settles it: the deliverable asserting its own Greek is native, and the grader's own impression of the prose, settle nothing.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every position, delta, timestamp, availability figure, and error count traces to the fixture or is arithmetic derived solely from fixture numbers with the derivation visible; no traffic, click, revenue, or conversion impact is quantified (the fixture has no traffic data), no index status, crawl result, or Google-side cause is asserted as observed (the fixture notes Search Console is inaccessible — checks are proposed, their results are not invented), no algorithm update is claimed as confirmed, and the data is labeled as what it is — a hand-kept log, a pasted uptime excerpt, and the developer's server-log count — never as connected-tool output.

evals.prompt: Full alert-system setup for petshop-mikroulis.gr, please. Our brief is in evals/files/alert-system-brief-petshop-mikroulis-en.md: the three people who actually exist here, the channels we use, our five priority-1 keywords, the traffic baseline our last analysis produced, and the manual AI-citation sheet Nikos fills in every Friday — including this week's results, which worry me. No tools are connected; the brief is everything. Design the complete system: alert categories with thresholds, who gets told what, when, through which channel, and what happens if nobody reacts. One thing — the template our old agency left routes P0 alerts to 'VP Marketing + DevOps + SEO Lead'; we are a three-person operation, so make the escalation real. And tell us what to do about this week's citation results.
evals.expected_output: A complete alert system scaled to the real team: routing and escalation defined only over Katerina, Nikos, and Thodoris with per-priority response times and an if-no-acknowledgement chain, channels matched to each person's stated availability (Thodoris's per-incident emergency phone reserved for site-down-class criticals), one priority-1 list serving both ranking and citation alerts with Tier-1 thresholds from the guide, this window's citation math done from the sheet — exactly 2 of the 5 priority-1 queries lost citations, firing the any-loss alert (band Warning, priority P1 under the priority-1 override) and explicitly not the 3-or-more loss cluster (band Critical, P0) — each loss routed to content-refresher's AI Overview recovery playbook, the «ενυδρείο για αρχάριους» win logged positive, the AI Overview appearance on «καλύτερη άμμος για γατάκια» graded Warning-band at P2, GEO thresholds labeled tunable weekly-window defaults, traffic thresholds derived from the brief's mean ≈1,967 / SD ≈13 with visible arithmetic, and zero invented people, roles, or numbers.
expectations: Routing and escalation are defined over the population that exists — the three named people (Katerina, Nikos, Thodoris) — with the inherited template's phantom roles (VP Marketing, DevOps, SEO Lead) adapted to real assignments rather than copied: every alert route and every escalation hop names one of the three, per-priority response times are stated on the P0-P3 axis consistent with the threshold guide's default map (P0 acknowledge <15 min and first action within 1 hour, P1 acknowledge <4 h and resolved same day, P2 within 48 hours, P3 weekly review/digest), no line in the configuration grades an alert 'High', 'Medium' or 'Low' — that third vocabulary was retired because its 'Critical' collided with the Critical threshold band — and an if-no-response escalation chain says who is contacted next and after how long.

Channel assignments respect the fixture's stated availability and cost constraints: P0 paths reach Katerina via phone/SMS (her any-time emergency channel) rather than the evenings-only email, Thodoris's per-incident-billed emergency line is reserved for site-down-class technical P0s while routine technical work rides the 48-hour email SLA, Nikos's Slack/email carries the business-hours load as the person in the tools daily, and P2/P3 alerts are batched into digests with a duplicate cooldown per the suppression rules instead of firing per event.

The one-list rule is enforced: the five priority-1 queries from the brief («petshop mikroulis», «ξηρά τροφή σκύλου», «τροφή σκύλου grain free», «τροφή κουταβιού», «άμμος γάτας») serve as both the Tier-1 ranking set and the priority-1 citation set per the skill's rule to 'maintain one list, not two', Tier-1 ranking thresholds from the guide's table (warning at drops >=3, critical at >=5) attach to exactly those five, and looser tiers cover everything else.

The citation-window math defines its count rule and population: counting priority-1 rows whose cited status flips from yes (w/c 27/07) to no (w/c 03/08), exactly 2 of the 5 priority-1 queries lost citations — «ξηρά τροφή σκύλου» and «τροφή κουταβιού» — which fires the any-priority-1-loss alert at its Warning band and P1 priority (logged per query or batched) — P1 rather than Warning's P2 default because the standing priority-1/Tier-1 override raises that row one level, which is how the templates define it ('Citation Lost (P1, band Warning)') — and explicitly NOT the 3-or-more loss-cluster grade (band Critical, priority P0), because the cluster rule requires 3+ losses in one window and 2 < 3 with the comparison visible; the response path hands each affected query and its cited source page (/trofes-skylou/) to content-refresher's AI Overview recovery playbook per the skill's citation-loss response rule.

The week's other events are graded per the event table with honest threshold labeling: the «ενυδρείο για αρχάριους» no-to-yes flip is logged as a positive/informational citation win with its earning page (/odigos-enydreio/) noted, not raised as a problem alert; the Google AI Overview appearing on «καλύτερη άμμος για γατάκια» is graded on both axes as a Warning-band event at P2 — the default map, with no override since that query is not on the priority-1 list — with the click-landscape rationale (either direction reshapes expected clicks for the query) and its competitor-sourced state reported from the fixture note without inventing which competitors; and the GEO/AI thresholds carried into the config are presented as tunable operational defaults on a weekly check window, to be calibrated against the site's own citation baseline, never as measured constants.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every name, channel, keyword, citation status, and baseline figure traces to the brief; traffic thresholds are arithmetic derived solely from the stated mean ≈1,967 / SD ≈13 via the guide's SD ladder with the multiplier and derivation visible; no citation rate, search volume, traffic value, competitor identity, or AI-answer status beyond what the sheet records is invented; and nothing is presented as fetched from a connected tool — the sheet and baseline are labeled as the user's manual data per the skill's source-labeling validation.

evals.prompt: We just launched keri-melisses.gr, a little Greek e-shop for beeswax candles — the site went live three weeks ago. Set up ranking and traffic drop alerts for us today: give me the actual threshold numbers for what counts as an abnormal drop, and the normal daily-traffic range we should expect, so I can put them straight into a spreadsheet. Nothing is connected and I have nothing to paste — we never saved any Search Console or analytics exports. You know what normal looks like for small e-shops, just fill the numbers in.
evals.expected_output: An honest baseline-missing hold instead of invented normals: the response states that no baseline exists for this site and that a normal range cannot be produced from nothing, refuses the 'you know what normal looks like' authorization, proposes the guide's baseline collection periods and the wide-threshold new-site posture, offers the generic starting defaults only as explicitly labeled defaults to recalibrate once weeks of real data exist, requests the skill's manual-data inputs, claims no tool reads, and delivers process — a collection plan and the setup framework — never site-specific findings.

The hold is forward-moving with no fake tool reads: the response claims no Search Console, analytics, or SEO-tool access and simulates no fetched data (observation-implying phrasings like 'your traffic currently averages…' fail), engages the manual-data mode per SKILL.md's Data Sources list (baseline metrics for thresholds, critical keywords or pages to monitor, priority levels and notification preferences, historical data for normal fluctuation ranges), and offers process while waiting — the alert-category framework, a data-collection checklist, and a recalibration date — never findings.
